requirement_text.REQ-456:
Approved by the user on 2026-10-06. No role in the roster reviews a process design before it is run: BA-<VERTICAL> authors scenarios and signs off its own vertical's results, and the only automated checks are structural. That breaks this project's rule that every producing step has a validating step. This entry defines the missing validator, following the precedent of REQ-359 (BA role) and REQ-361 (PRODUCT-OWNER): role file, roster entries, workflow step, artefact. Write the role file so a weak model can execute it: numbered procedure, closed checklists, closed verdict values, examples.
BUILDS: 1. .claude/agents/process-auditor.md. AGENT_ID PROCESS-AUDITOR. Independence: it never authors or edits a definition, a scenario, a seed script or the roster, and never signs off run results. Inputs: the process definitions and forms of one scope (vertical or platform), its scenarios, test/fixtures/uat/actors.yaml, the seed scripts, docs/roles.md, and the validator output of REQ-455. It reads; it does not run a UAT. Checklist, each item answered YES, NO or NOT_APPLICABLE with evidence: A. Missing business paths: for every approval or decision, is there a rejection outcome, a rework or correction loop where the business needs one, and an end for each outcome; for every human task, what happens if nobody acts (timer, escalation or an explicit statement that waiting forever is intended). B. Separation of duties: can the same person both request and approve, or both enter and verify, given the roles the tasks route to and the roster. C. Data on some paths only: a decision reads a value that at least one path to it does not collect (the certain case is REQ-455's). D. Consistency inside the scope: every scenario step corresponds to a step the process has and the reverse for every human task; every role a task routes to has an actor in the roster; every actor has the least built-in role for its steps (docs/roles.md). E. Access: the scenarios contain a refusal step for each sensitive action (approve, pay, see personal data, change users); no admin actor performs ordinary business steps; no tenant actor depends on a platform permission. F. Consistency across scopes: the same business concept (for example an approval with a limit) is not modelled in two incompatible ways without a stated reason. Verdict PASS, PASS_WITH_FINDINGS or FAIL; any BLOCKER finding is FAIL. Findings state the business consequence in plain language and are handed to ORCH, which files them per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md. 2. Artefact test/uat-reports/process-audit-<scope>-<run_id>.yaml with a schema in the role file: scope, audited inputs with a content digest of each file, the checklist answers, findings (id, severity, checklist item, business description, affected definition or scenario, suggested owner), verdict. 3. docs/agents/workflows/WF-05_uat_run.md: a new step between environment preparation and the run. ORCH dispatches PROCESS-AUDITOR for a scope when no audit artefact exists whose input digests match the current files; an unchanged scope is not re-audited. A FAIL verdict blocks UAT-RUNNER for that scope only. This keeps the gate off the per-run path when nothing changed. 4. docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md (roster row, capability row: read yes, write process-audit reports only, no shell beyond read-only search, no merge), docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md (routing and the gate), CLAUDE.md roster table. 5. .claude/agents/product-owner.md: reads the audit verdicts of the run's scopes; a scope with no PASS or PASS_WITH_FINDINGS audit is not APPROVED.
OPEN QUESTIONS: Model for this agent. Default: the same default as the other validating roles; no model override in the role file. | Whether SECURITY-REVIEWER also reviews seed scripts. Default: PROCESS-AUDITOR covers scenarios, roster and seed-script role use under checklist E; SECURITY-REVIEWER stays on code and is called only through a finding.
